rawCommits.subject: fix(ci): pass shell:true on Windows so npm.cmd stops failing PRs with EINVAL
rawCommits.body:
Node 18.20.2+/20.12.2+/21.7.3+/22+ refuses to spawn `.cmd`/`.bat` shims
without `shell: true` (CVE-2024-27980). On Windows our parity helpers
rewrite `npm`/`npx` to `npm.cmd`/`npx.cmd`, so every Windows CI lane in
desktop-validate failed at the very first `npm ci` with
`spawnSync npm.cmd EINVAL` before the shim was ever launched. This blocked
community PRs that couldn't bypass the required Windows check.

Add a `needsShell` helper scoped to the same commands `commandName`
rewrites and pass it through to all three spawnSync sites (run, capture,
tryCapture). Keep it scoped to npm/npx so we don't opt every spawn into
shell-quoting risk; current call sites only pass simple tokens and plain
paths, which cmd.exe parses safely.

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): coerce non-object tool_use.input to a marker before persist
rawCommits.body:
Adds a defense-in-depth guard so a buggy or older upstream harness can
never poison the persisted assistant turn with a `tool_use.input` that
is anything other than a JSON object. Anthropic rejects such history
with 400 `messages.N.content.M.tool_use.input: Input should be an
object`, which previously silently broke every subsequent turn in the
session and required the user to restart the chat.

Changes in `apps/aura-os-server/src/handlers/agents/chat/persist_task_dispatch.rs`:
- New `coerce_tool_use_input_to_object` helper: objects pass through,
  null -> `{}`, anything else (string, array, number, bool) is logged
  at `error` and replaced with a structured `_normalized` marker that
  records the original type and byte size for forensics.
- `handle_tool_call_snapshot` now coerces the snapshot input before
  both updating the in-memory block and writing the persisted event,
  so the corruption can never round-trip through the database.
- `backfill_null_tool_use_input` is renamed to `normalize_tool_use_input`
  and broadened to catch the same non-object case at the
  tool_result boundary (the long-standing null backfill is preserved).

Changes in `conversions/session_history/in_flight.rs`:
- `apply_tool_call_snapshot` mirrors the same normalization when
  rebuilding an in-flight turn from already-persisted events, so even
  sessions saved by an older harness build replay cleanly after refresh.

Adds 9 unit tests in `persist_task_dispatch` covering the object/null/
string/array cases plus the existing append/update flow, and a
regression test in `conversions/tests/in_flight.rs` that round-trips a
persisted string-typed snapshot through reconstruction and asserts the
emitted ToolUse input is a JSON object carrying the normalization
marker.

Pairs with aura-harness fix(compaction) 63db417 which stops the
upstream `truncate_messages_for_storage` from stringifying oversized
tool_use inputs in the first place.

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): arm new-chat pin on the fresh-canvas partition
rawCommits.body:
After the per-session stream lane refactor, `useFreshCanvas.newChat()`
wrote `nextSendStartsNewSession` to the partition keyed by the panel's
current session id, then dropped `?session=` from the URL. The next
send fired on the `:fresh` partition and read `false` — so the wire
flag became `new_session=false`, the server reused the existing
session via `existing_session_for_agent`, `SessionReady` snapped the
URL back, and `generate_session_title` skipped because the user
message was no longer the first in the storage session. User-visible
symptoms: "+ New chat" reverted to a previous chat and the new chat
never got a Haiku-style title.

Both chat surfaces now target the lane's fresh-canvas partition key
directly so the pin lands on the partition the post-+ send actually
reads from. `useChatStream` writes to
`keyForProjectSession(projectId, agentInstanceId, null)`, and
`useAgentChatStream` writes to `keyForAgentSession(agentId, null)`
via a new per-key `nextSendStartsNewSession` field on
`PartitionAgentReplay` (replacing the per-hook ref that the previous
`core.key`-keyed reset effect had to aggressively wipe to prevent
agent-swap leaks). Both flips are covered by new regression tests
that mount with a real `sessionId`, arm the pin, rerender with
`sessionId: null`, and assert the next send POSTs `new_session=true`.

unconditionally pairing with `setActiveTab("specs")`. In the Projects

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): release turn slot and cancel harness on Stop / refresh
rawCommits.body:
Pressing Stop on a chat turn — especially a long-running plan-mode
`generate_specs` turn — used to leave the per-partition turn slot
held server-side because the client only aborted its SSE reader and
no `InboundMessage::Cancel` was ever forwarded to the harness. The
warm `ChatSession` survived a refresh (`commands_tx` still open), so
the next user message blocked on `acquire_turn_slot` until the 90s
SSE idle timeout fired `SSEIdleTimeoutError` with no actionable
error surfaced. After plan-mode -> code-mode this looked like the
chat had silently wedged.

Wires up a coordinated client + server cleanup path:

- `spawn_turn_slot_release` now selects on a
  `oneshot::Receiver<HarnessCommandSender>` in addition to the
  broadcast terminal-event arm. When the SSE stream is dropped (Stop
  or refresh) the drop guard fires the oneshot, the sentinel
  forwards `HarnessInbound::Cancel`, and releases the slot. The
  `biased` select keeps the happy-path terminal-event arm winning
  when the harness ends normally.
- `streaming::open_harness_chat_stream` plumbs `commands_tx` through
  `SessionForTurn` and wraps the SSE body in `SseDropGuardStream`,
  which fires the oneshot exactly once when axum drops the response.
- New `POST /api/agents/:agent_id/cancel-turn` and
  `POST /api/projects/:project_id/agents/:agent_instance_id/cancel-turn`
  endpoints sweep every live `ChatSession` on the partition, forward
  Cancel, and evict the warm sessions so the next send cold-starts
  cleanly. Idempotent: 204 even when nothing is in flight.
- `stopStreaming` in both `use-chat-stream` and
  `use-agent-chat-stream` now POSTs the new endpoint fire-and-forget
  before the existing `AbortController.abort()`. The server-side
  drop guard is the safety net if this POST never lands.

Tests: extends the `turn_slot` suite with the new oneshot path and
adds a `setup` registry-only worker test to pin the partition-prefix
sweep + Cancel forwarding contract; the frontend gets a regression
guard that `stopStreaming` POSTs `cancel-turn` and swallows network
failures.

persistence pipeline the chat agent uses, via a thin sibling

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): treat tool_call_snapshot mid-stream strings as the streaming protocol, not corruption
rawCommits.body:
The aura-protocol ToolCallSnapshot.input field carries Anthropic's
input_json_delta accumulator — a Value::String that grows byte-by-byte
across many small chunks until the closing brace arrives and the final
snapshot lands as a Value::Object. The previous normalize logic flagged
every intermediate snapshot as upstream corruption, spamming the error
log with one ERROR per partial chunk (the live log showed sizes
2 -> 9 -> 11 -> 16 -> 27 -> 39 -> 51 -> 60 -> 70 -> 79 for one tool_use)
and persisting throwaway _normalized placeholders to the SessionEvent
stream on every step.

- persist_task_dispatch::normalize::coerce_tool_use_input_with_status
  now classifies Value::String as the streaming case: tries to parse it
  as JSON; if a complete object lands, uses it as the canonical input;
  otherwise returns a {} placeholder + is_streaming=true and logs at
  trace (not error). The ERROR path is reserved for Array/Number/Bool,
  which Anthropic never emits for tool input.
- persist_task_dispatch::tool::handle_tool_call_snapshot returns early
  when is_streaming=true, skipping both the content_blocks mutation and
  the persist_event write. The final snapshot still lands normally, so
  end state is identical; live UI is unaffected because SSE consumers
  read directly from the harness broadcast.
- agents::conversions::session_history::in_flight::apply_tool_call_snapshot
  parses complete-object string snapshots through; unparseable strings
  (legacy historical data only — post-fix persistence never writes them)
  keep the existing _normalized marker so forensics are preserved.

against the post-G5b baseline (8 lib + 10 lib-test + 2 integration

width (e.g. 320), so the computed `available` overshot the real budget by
that amount and the sidekick ended up much wider than the main panel.

Measure `offsetWidth` on the main panel host AND a new ref to the sidekick
lane DOM, then split that combined visible budget in half. Preserve the
current outer-vs-CSS-width delta so the math is correct under either
`box-sizing` setting (ZUI's base reset applies `border-box` globally, but
the delta-based form is robust either way).

rawCommits.subject: fix(automation-bar): keep Play visible with a spinning ring while the loop runs
rawCommits.body:
Replacing the Play icon with a Loader2 spinner during
`starting`/`preparing` and then dropping the spinner once `active`
arrived left a bare Play icon on a still-running loop — the user
read that as "the run is off" even when the harness was actively
working. The button title flipping from "Start" to "Resume" only
fires for the explicit `paused` branch, so the rest of the time the
affordance looked idle.

Keep the Play glyph rendered at all times and overlay an absolutely-
positioned SVG progress ring around it whenever the loop is doing
work (`starting`, `preparing`, or `active`). The ring mirrors
`<LoopProgress>`'s geometry and cadence (~70% arc, 1.1s linear) so
loop activity reads the same wherever it surfaces. The disabled
opacity rule is selectively overridden on the active Play button so
the icon + ring stay legible (the button remains
non-interactive — clicking Start while running is meaningless — but
the visual is informational, not faded out).

Regression tests pin the new contract:
- Play icon + progress ring present while the loop is active.
- No ring when idle.
- No ring when paused, so the now-meaningful Resume affordance
  reads as a real button.

rawCommits.subject: fix(ui): correct sidekick split math; toggle off restores default width
rawCommits.body:
Two fixes for the split-screen toggle:

1. Drop the delta correction in `computeSplitTargetWidth`. ZUI applies
   `box-sizing: border-box` globally (vendor/zui/src/styles/base.css), so
   the lane's CSS width and `offsetWidth` are already equal. The previous
   `delta = sidekickOuter - controls.getSize()` correction broke the
   collapsed-sidekick case because `sidekickOuter` is 0 while
   `controls.getSize()` still returns the open width, pushing the target
   to `budget/2 + openWidth` and making the sidekick much wider than
   half. The simple `Math.floor((mainOuter + sidekickOuter) / 2)` formula
   handles the collapsed case correctly (budget == mainOuter, target ==
   mainOuter/2 after expand).

2. Toggling split OFF now restores `DEFAULT_SIDEKICK_WIDTH` (320) and
   persists it, instead of restoring whatever the user had drag-resized
   to previously. Both toggle states are now deterministic defaults:
   ON = 50/50 of the current main+sidekick area; OFF = the standard 320px
   sidekick width.

rawCommits.subject: fix(dev-loop): surface harness stop failures instead of silently lying
rawCommits.body:
When the harness `POST /automaton/:id/stop` request failed (harness
unreachable, wrong url, non-success response), the failure was buried
in a `warn!` log and the OS-side registry was cleared anyway, so the
UI optimistically returned to idle while the harness automaton kept
running. This made "UI says stopped but harness is still going"
effectively invisible.

For Stop specifically, log the failure at `error!` with
`harness_base_url` and the error string, and forward the error in the
`loop_stopped` domain event payload as `harness_error` so the
streaming debug log (and any UI toast wired to it) makes the state
divergence visible.

Preserves the intentional "clear local registry even when harness is
unreachable" contract (see `loop_stop_clears_registry_even_when_
harness_unreachable`) so the UI can still recover when the harness is
genuinely dead.

Existing `loop_stop` tests still pass; payload shape is additive
(extra `harness_error` field on failure, unchanged `{}` on success).

rawCommits.subject: refactor(automation-ui): fold Play + progress ring into one SVG so the loop indicator is pixel-perfect concentric
rawCommits.body:
The previous overlay design — render a lucide `<Play size={14}>`,
then absolutely-position a sibling ring SVG over it with
`inset: -3px` — drifted inside the zui Button's icon slot. The
overlay span wasn't anchoring to the wrap the way we assumed
(likely because the Button wraps the icon in its own slot
element), and the two glyphs ended up rendering side-by-side
instead of stacking. From a user's perspective: "play triangle,
then a broken circle" instead of "play with a ring around it".

Replace both `AutomationBar.PlayWithProgressRing` and
`SidekickTaskbar.TabIconWithProgressRing` with a single shared
`<PlayLoopGlyph>` component that draws the lucide Play polygon
*and* the (optional) rotating progress ring in **one SVG**. Both
shapes share one coordinate system, one transform, one
accessible role — there is no positioning concern to drift.

Geometry choices that make the indicator look right:

- `viewBox="0 0 24 24"` mirrors lucide's stock Play viewBox; the
  polygon path is the unchanged `"6 3 20 12 6 21 6 3"` so the
  Play glyph stays visually identical to a plain
  `<Play size={size}>` at any rendered size.
- Ring is centred at `(10.67, 12)` — the **centroid** of the
  triangle rather than its bbox centre. A right-pointing
  triangle has its visual weight on the left flat edge, so
  centring the ring on the centroid lines it up with the
  perceived centre of the play (same trick YouTube/Spotify use
  for their circular play buttons).
- Ring radius is `16` viewBox units, comfortably outside the
  play's ~7-unit half-extent so the two never crowd each other.
  At r=16 the ring extends past the 24-unit viewBox and
  `style={{ overflow: 'visible' }}` lets it draw into the
  button's padding without enlarging the SVG element itself
  (button physical size is unchanged, the user wanted just the
  circle bigger).
- Faint full background ring + brighter spinning accent arc, so
  the rotation reads as "wedge moving around a complete track"
  instead of "broken circle floating next to the play".
- Rotation uses `transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin:
  center` so the arc spins around the circle's own bbox centre
  (`(10.67, 12)` in viewBox units) — the default SVG
  `transform-origin: 0 0` would have spun it around the
  top-left of the icon, which is why earlier CSS-only attempts
  produced a circle that wobbled diagonally instead of
  spinning in place.

Surfaces touched:

- New shared component: `interface/src/components/PlayLoopGlyph/{PlayLoopGlyph.tsx,PlayLoopGlyph.module.css,index.ts}`.
- `AutomationBar.tsx`: drop the inline `PlayWithProgressRing`,
  use `<PlayLoopGlyph active={loopWorking} size={14}>`. Drop the
  obsolete `.playIconWrap`, `.playProgressRing`, and `spinRing`
  keyframe from `AutomationBar.module.css`; keep
  `.playButtonActive` (the disabled-state opacity override) and
  add an `overflow: visible` rule for the button so the ring is
  not clipped by any ancestor `overflow: hidden`.
- `SidekickTaskbar.tsx`: drop the inline
  `TabIconWithProgressRing`, use `<PlayLoopGlyph active={runActive} size={16}>`
  on the Run tab. Drop the obsolete `.tabIconWithProgressRing`,
  `.tabProgressRing`, and `spinTabRing` keyframe from
  `Sidekick.module.css`.
- Tests: `AutomationBar.test.tsx` and `SidekickTaskbar.test.tsx`
  now look for the polygon path (`svg polygon`) instead of a
  `svg.lucide-play` class (since the polygon is drawn inline by
  PlayLoopGlyph, not by lucide), and use the unified
  `data-testid="play-loop-ring"` for the ring (was
  `play-progress-ring` / `tab-progress-ring`).

Verification: 28/28 affected tests pass (`AutomationBar`,
`SidekickTaskbar`, `PlayLoopGlyph`); `tsc --noEmit` is clean.

rawCommits.subject: fix(interface): hoist nested-paren tool markers into Block cards
rawCommits.body:
Tool markers like
`[tool: search_code(pub fn (ack|len), context=1) -> ok]` were leaking
through as raw text in the sidekick Run pane (and any other surface
that renders LLM prose) because three separate copies of the marker
regex used `[^)]*` for the argument capture. That class stops at the
first inner `)`, so as soon as the arg contained nested parens the
whole marker failed to match and fell through to `SegmentedContent`
as literal markdown instead of hoisting into a Block card.

Switch the argument capture to a lazy, marker-bounded class
(`[^\]\r\n]*?`) in all three sites:

- `interface/src/utils/tool-markers.ts` (primary `LLMOutput` ->
  `ActivityTimeline` path used by `MessageBubble`,
  `CompletedTaskOutput`, `ActiveTaskStream`, `LLMStreamOutput`)
- `interface/src/utils/derive-activity.ts` (`IterationBar` complexity
  dots and `TaskPreview` activity rows)
- `interface/src/apps/chat/components/FormattedRawOutput/FormattedRawOutput.tsx`
  (alternate raw-output renderer)

Also accept the unicode arrow (U+2192) in the two latter regexes;
the server-emitted form is the unicode arrow and only
`tool-markers.ts` recognized it before. Add nested-paren coverage to
each test file plus a brand-new `FormattedRawOutput` render test so
the three regexes stay in lockstep.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(loop): show per-task spinner during active automation runs
rawCommits.body:
Two independent races conspired to leave the actively-running task in
the Sidekick > Tasks tree rendered as a hollow circle instead of a
spinner during automation runs:

1. Backend: the `LoopHandle::transition` ~4 Hz throttle could swallow
   the very first `set_current_task` after `LoopRegistry::open`. That
   call only mutates `current_task_id` and leaves `status = Starting`,
   so neither `status_changed` nor `status_is_terminal` was true; the
   `last_published_ms` was seeded with the open timestamp so
   `elapsed_ms` was well under the 250ms window. The
   `LoopActivityChanged` carrying `current_task_id` was therefore never
   broadcast, and the frontend's `selectTaskActivity` filter could not
   bind `LoopProgress` to the row. Add a `task_changed` bypass
   alongside the existing status/terminal bypasses. Covered by a new
   `set_current_task_bypasses_throttle_even_without_status_change`
   regression test on the loop registry.

2. Frontend: `displayStatus` only knew how to *downgrade* a stuck
   `in_progress` row to `ready`; it never *upgraded* a `ready` task
   that the server already reported as live (typical right after page
   refresh during a run, or in the gap between `task_started`
   delivery and the storage transition). Extract the rule into a
   shared `getTaskDisplayStatus` helper that handles both directions
   and replace the four inline copies (TaskList, ProjectWorkView,
   ProjectTasksView, TaskFeed) so all four surfaces stay in lockstep.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(interface): union live-task-ids with loop-activity store for spinner
rawCommits.body:
The per-row task spinner ("is this task being worked on right now")
needs three independent signals to all be in sync:

  1. useLiveTaskIdsStore populated by task_started WS events and
     /loop/status.active_tasks polls
  2. task.status === "in_progress" from storage / task_saved
  3. useLoopActivityStore.loops[*].activity.current_task_id updated
     by LoopActivityChanged WS broadcasts

The previous fix added a backend throttle bypass so signal #3 always
fires immediately on current_task_id changes, plus a frontend helper
that upgrades ready -> in_progress whenever signal #1 reports the
task as live. But the helper only consulted signal #1, so a row whose
task_started subscriber happened to be unmounted (or whose
/loop/status poll returned an empty active_tasks because the
registry hadn't been written yet) would still render a hollow circle
even though signal #3 already had the right current_task_id.

Add a selectActiveTaskIdsForProject selector to the loop-activity
store and a useEffectiveLiveTaskIdsForProject hook that unions both
sources, then route TaskList / TaskFeed / mobile views through it.
Now signal #1 OR signal #3 (independently) is enough to upgrade the
display status to in_progress.

Also adds:

  * window.__AURA_DEBUG_TASK_STATUS__ = true toggle that logs every
    getTaskDisplayStatus call's inputs + result for debugging future
    spinner regressions.
  * window.__AURA_DEBUG_STORES__ (dev-only) exposing the
    live-task-ids and loop-activity stores so DevTools can inspect
    them without source-map digging.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(dev-loop): auto-retry harness research-loop aborts at both classifier and gate layers
rawCommits.body:
The aura-os retry path was designed assuming all restartable failures originate from tool-call errors. Task-shape failures like "task completed without any file operations - completion not verified" (emitted by the aura-harness post-hoc completion gate) fall through two consecutive guards: the classifier doesn't recognise the reason, and even if it did, the task-level retry gate requires tool-call budget exhaustion before firing.

Two coordinated changes:
- Extend is_completion_contract_failure (both harness signals + server mirror) and add is_research_loop_abort in the automation classifier family. classify_restart_reason now returns Some("research_loop") for the verdict.
- Relax the tool-budget gate in maybe_apply_task_level_retry so it only blocks when there has actually been a per-tool failure for the task. For task-shape failures (zero recorded tool retries) the gate now falls through to the task-level budget, which then issues safe_transition(Failed -> Ready) up to TASK_LEVEL_RETRY_BUDGET=3.

Verified against bundle 20260519_184649 / task 5dade068 (the OutboxPump task), where the other 6 tasks in the same run completed first-try and a fresh-context retry would have very likely succeeded.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: refactor(interface): unify live-task-ids onto loop-activity store
rawCommits.body:
The "is this task being worked on right now" signal lived in two
parallel zustand stores fed by different code paths:

- useLiveTaskIdsStore: hand-mirrored from task_started / task_completed
  / task_failed WS subscribers in useTaskListData + useMobileTasks,
  plus a /loop/status.active_tasks poll on mount/reconnect.
- useLoopActivityStore: fed by LoopOpened / LoopActivityChanged /
  LoopEnded WS broadcasts, plus /api/loops snapshot on reconnect.

Both answered the same question and could diverge — that's how the
per-row spinner regressed in the first place. Consolidate onto
useLoopActivityStore as the single source of truth:

- live-task-ids-store now exposes only useLiveTaskIdsForProject as a
  thin derived view over selectActiveTaskIdsForProject. The underlying
  Map state, addLive/removeLive/clearProject mutators, and the
  hydrateFromLoopStatus path are gone.
- useTaskListData drops its private mirror — TaskStarted / TaskCompleted
  / TaskFailed handlers only patch task status now; LoopStopped /
  LoopPaused / LoopFinished only refetch task list.
- useMobileTasks loses the same mirror.
- TaskFeed reads from the unified hook directly (no useEffective merge).
- useAutomationStatus drops the live-task-ids hydration in
  hydrateUiFromLoopStartResponse; loop_opened + loop_activity_changed
  arrive within a frame and write current_task_id straight onto the
  loop-activity store.

Also lock in the contract with a regression test
(stores/live-task-ids-store.test.ts) covering the active-only filter,
project scoping, multi-loop merging, transition to current_task_id
null, and LoopEnded removal.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rendered.title: Parallel chat sessions, a resilient automation loop, and a clearer Run affordance
rendered.intro: Today's nightly lands the long-running parallel-session-chats work end-to-end, hardens the dev-loop with shared retry budgets and orphan recovery, and sharpens the sidekick's automation UI — including a redesigned play-with-progress-ring indicator and a per-task spinner that finally stays in sync with what the harness is actually doing.

entries.title: Parallel chat sessions on the same agent instance
entries.summary: Per-session partitioning lands across server harness keys and client stream lanes so two sessions of the same agent can stream simultaneously without sharing state.

items.text: Chat sessions are now partitioned by storage session id end-to-end: the harness session key carries an optional third segment, the server opens distinct ChatSession entries and turn slots per session, and reset sweeps target the full per-session prefix so old sessions and mutexes no longer leak.

The interface keys every chat stream lane by session id for both project and standalone agent chat, with a migration helper that carries state across the fresh-canvas→real and auto-fork session flips, plus a per-session streaming indicator in the SessionsList sidebar.

Followup cleanup consolidates per-partition state into a single PartitionRegistry, unifies auto-retry state across chat surfaces, and tightens the server's session_id chain to a typed SessionId from ingress to persistence — closing the parse-back hole the new partitioning had exposed.
New projects now appear at the top of the left menu instead of the bottom, and the model picker menu renders through a body portal so adjacent panels can no longer clip it.
A Windows CI fix passes shell:true through the parity helpers so npm.cmd no longer aborts every Windows lane with EINVAL, unblocking community PRs against the required Desktop check.

entries.title: Dev-loop resilience, Stop semantics, and the new aura-os-automation crate
entries.summary: A coordinated push hardens the automation loop with shared retry budgets and orphan recovery, fixes a wedged-after-Stop chat, and absorbs corrupt tool history so Anthropic 400s stop poisoning sessions.

items.text: A new aura-os-automation crate now owns transient/restart/push classifiers, retry budgets, task-failure synthesis, tool- and task-level retry trackers, and an InProgress orphan sweep at loop start; the dev-loop wires these in so silent task failures get a reason, retries respect a shared budget, mid-run crashes resume cleanly, and the stalled spinner from stale event-kind matching is gone.

Pressing Stop (or refreshing) now POSTs a new cancel-turn endpoint and a server-side drop guard forwards Cancel to the harness and releases the per-partition turn slot — fixing the case where the next message hung for 90s on a wedged warm session after plan-mode → code-mode.

Chat history is now defended against malformed tool blocks: tool_use.input is coerced to an object before persist, duplicate tool_result blocks are deduped at replay with the wire-level tool_use_id, and the harness distinguishes Timeout/StreamClosed from a clean Done so early disconnects surface as real failures.

Dev-loop harness events now persist through the same SessionEvent pipeline as chat, so replays inherit dangling-tool-use stripping, recent-window caps, blob truncation, and the new parallel-result dedupe.

Several chat UX papercuts are fixed: '+ New chat' now actually starts a new session and gets a Haiku-style title, Plan mode no longer yanks the sidekick off the Sessions tab, untouched agents restore the last-picked model, deleting a stale pending Spec stops showing 'Bad Request', and the project's Add Agent flow dismisses cleanly without creating duplicates.

Plan mode regains the planner toolkit — create/update/delete/transition_task are now surfaced so the planner can organize work without starting it — while execution tools (run_task, task_done, submit_plan) stay structurally off.
The pinned 'cooking' indicator gets a proper backdrop and ListBlock's header is aligned with SpecBlock so the hover copy affordance no longer overlaps the item count.

Several oversized server and harness modules are split along responsibility boundaries (agent/chat, dev_loop adapter/streaming/signals, harness automaton_client) to land under the 500-line cap without changing public paths or runtime behavior.

entries.title: Streaming tool-call snapshots stop being treated as corruption
entries.summary: The persistence layer now recognizes Anthropic's input_json_delta accumulator as a streaming protocol rather than logging every partial chunk as upstream corruption.

items.text: Mid-stream string tool_use.input values are parsed when complete and skipped at trace level when partial, eliminating the per-chunk ERROR spam and the throwaway _normalized placeholders that previously littered the session event stream. The final object snapshot still lands and persists normally.

entries.title: Automation model picker, split-screen sidekick, and per-task spinner binding
entries.summary: The sidekick gains a deliberate model selector and a 50/50 split toggle, while a backend fix finally binds the per-task spinner to the live task during automation runs.

items.text: An AutomationBar model picker — also surfaced in the Run pane header — lets each project pick a deliberate chat model for loop runs, persisted per project and locked once the loop is starting/active/paused so no one can pretend to swap mid-run.

A new titlebar Columns2 button toggles a 50/50 split between the main panel and the sidekick lane, persisted across reloads, with ResizeObserver-driven rebalancing, auto-expand when the sidekick is collapsed, and a deterministic restore to the standard 320px width when toggled off.

The dev-loop forwarder now publishes the typed current_task_id onto LoopActivity so per-task spinners in TaskList can bind, fixing the case where the run looked idle even while the harness was actively working.

The Play button on the AutomationBar and the Run tab in SidekickTaskbar keep the play glyph visible at all times and overlay a rotating progress ring while the loop is active, so users can still find the control during a live run.

The dev-loop's automation crate now also re-readies cross-run Failed tasks at loop start (gated by the shared task-level retry budget), and dev-loop agents are spliced with the InvokeProcess capability so cargo check/test no longer burn turns on permission errors.

The pinned cooking indicator is realigned with the chat content edge and the same gradient backdrop is applied to the sidekick Run pane and Tasks-tab Live Output so trailing rows stop bleeding through the shimmer.

entries.title: Stop failures no longer lie about loop state
entries.summary: When the harness rejects or drops a stop request, the dev-loop now logs it at error and forwards the failure in the loop_stopped payload instead of optimistically reporting idle.

items.text: POST /automaton/:id/stop failures are emitted as harness_error on the loop_stopped event with the harness base URL, so the UI can surface 'UI says stopped but harness is still going' instead of hiding it in a warn log — while preserving the contract that the local registry still clears when the harness is genuinely unreachable.

entries.title: Unified Play/loop indicator and a per-task spinner that finally tracks reality
entries.summary: An afternoon polish pass replaces the drifting overlay icons with a single shared glyph, then fixes the remaining races that left the actively-running task rendered as a hollow circle.

items.text: A new shared PlayLoopGlyph component draws the play polygon and the optional spinning progress ring inside one SVG centred on the triangle's centroid, replacing the previous fragile absolute-overlay approach across both AutomationBar and SidekickTaskbar; the ring now also takes its colour from the active theme accent instead of a fixed blue.

A backend throttle bypass ensures the very first set_current_task always broadcasts, a shared getTaskDisplayStatus helper now upgrades ready→in_progress when the server reports the task as live, and the live-task signal is unified onto the loop-activity store so TaskList, TaskFeed, ProjectWorkView, and mobile views all stay in lockstep.

Tool markers with nested parentheses like search_code(pub fn (ack|len), context=1) now hoist into Block cards across LLMOutput, derive-activity, and FormattedRawOutput instead of leaking through as raw text.

The dev-loop classifier now recognises harness research-loop aborts and 'task completed without any file operations' shape failures, and the task-level retry gate falls through to its own budget when there's no tool-call history — letting these task-shape failures retry up to three times instead of getting stuck on the first crash.
The pinned cooking indicator is lifted above the input bar's ModeSelector row on both desktop and mobile so the Code/Plan/Image/3D pills are no longer covered by its backdrop.

highlights: Two sessions on the same agent now stream concurrently end-to-end
Dev-loop retries, recovers orphans, and re-readies failed tasks across runs
Stop reliably cancels the harness and releases the turn slot
New split-screen sidekick toggle and a per-project automation model picker
Play button keeps a concentric progress ring while the loop runs
